diagnosis: Repeated rounded bead offsets and full layer unions dominated native validation after the original branch geometry was complete.
Interface connector visibility repeatedly prepared identical native clip masks and evaluated independent visibility edges serially.
Bridge direction scores were independent but serial; candidate straight bridges repeatedly ran complete geometric bearing checks.
corrections: Bound exact geometry-content caches using the existing shared live RAM allowance, invalidate mutable footprints after every relevant path mutation, and retain uncached behavior on constrained or unknown-memory hosts.
Keep native clipping, original candidate order, Dijkstra settlement and tie handling; use conservative bounds, immutable native clip preparation and memory-bounded independent visibility queries.
Evaluate bridge directions independently with bounded workers, preserve each score summation order, and keep the original final score selection order.
Use positive-only actual-material certificates for backed curves and two-ended straight bridges; all ambiguous, curved-cantilever or boundary cases fall back to original native checks.
Build earlier physical layer masks only for actual overlapping queries, retain existing model/contact/collision rules and leave every accepted process parameter unchanged.

invariants.contact_preservation: Repeated test2 native instructions and bead metadata are exactly equal to the previously verified 0.17mm contact/rim output. Native contact and curved-floor regressions also pass.

remaining_work: The requested 10x target is not met. The verified result is the measured clean paired speedup only; broader pipeline optimization would require further source-bound validation.
